BBC News live

Americans are electing members of Congress, which is made up of the House of Representatives and the Senate. All 435 House seats are up for election. In the Senate, only 35 of 100 seats are being contested because senators serve six-year terms. This results tracker shows both the races being decided now and the 65 seats that are not up for election this year - 34 held by Democrats and 31 by Republicans.

The Democrats win the Senate and the House in US midterm elections, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency

Trump says the Democrats \"did a good job\" - and acknowledges the Iran war, and higher fuel prices, played a part in the defeat

There is no mystery about why this happened, writes our North America editor - voters are angry about the cost of living, and blame the president

In the Senate race, Democrats picked up a string of victories in Republican strongholds, including Texas, Ohio, and Kansas - which last elected a Democrat almost 100 years ago

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory, telling voters: \"You took a chance on the unlikeliest of candidates\" - he'll be the first Muslim to serve in the US Senate

With control of Congress, Democrats will be able to frustrate President Trump's plans for the next two years - and could even try to impeach him for a third time

The Michigan Senate seat is projected to go to the Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, CBS says.

Claiming victory a little earlier, El-Sayed told supporters: \"You took a chance on the unlikeliest of candidates... Michigan, I cannot wait to serve you.\"

El-Sayed will be the first Muslim to serve in the US Senate.

El-Sayed projected to win Michigan Senate seat - CBS

Will the results of the midterms have consequences for the Kremlin?

\"President Trump will remain president until the end of his term and will carry out his foreign policy,\" President Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov told me on Monday.

The message seemed to be: whatever the outcome, Moscow is expecting business as usual.

President Trump may not have delivered exactly what Russia wants – a signed and sealed peace deal on Ukraine on Russia’s terms – but his foreign policy has produced plenty of positives for the Kremlin.

The US president recently froze some anti-Russia sanctions, agreed to buy Russian diesel and he has been far more critical of Volodymr Zelensky than of Vladimir Putin.

But earlier this week Russia’s Nezavisimaya Gazeta newspaper predicted that, if the Republicans lost control of Congress, Donald Trump would “get bogged down in numerous investigations initiated by the Democrats\" and that it was \"unlikely he’ll be able to pursue the policies he considers right, including on Russia.\"

What these results mean for US-Russia relations

Former President Barack Obama says his party's sweeping victory is evidence that Americans want change.

Writing on X, Obama says: \"Tonight, the American people sent a clear message — they want a politics that brings people together rather than divides them, and leaders who offer concrete solutions to the challenges they face.\"

Obama has campaigned with several Democratic candidates in swing states like Michigan and Georgia.

He adds: \"Our job now is to roll up our sleeves, make changes wherever we have the power to do so, prevent further damage, and lay the groundwork for the future.\"

Obama says Americans have sent a 'clear message'

The Republican Party is projected to have won the Senate contests in Idaho and Montana, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

Kurt Alme is projected to have won for the Republicans in Montana, with Jim Risch retaining his seat in Idaho.

Republicans projected to hold Idaho and Montana Senate seats - CBS

It's been an extraordinary night for the Democrats in the US midterms.

The BBC's US partner CBS News projected the Democrats would win the House just after 03:00 GMT on Wednesday (22:00 EST Tuesday).

The results in the Senate are beyond what the Democrats would have expected, with a series of wins in Republican strongholds - including South Carolina, Kansas, Texas, Iowa and Ohio.

There are still two toss-up seats to come in Alaska and Maine. Even Mississippi is now on a knife edge, according to CBS News. Here's a look at where things stand in the key battlegrounds:

How America has voted so far - in maps and charts

Abdul El-Sayed’s supporters went wild when he took the stage to celebrate his claimed victory. (As a reminder, votes are still being counted and a winner is not yet projected.)

Their cheers were deafening and they chanted his name in jubilation.

A sea of iPhones were held up to take in this moment of history: a Muslim man who could be elected to the Senate. Several people in the crowd embraced, filled with emotion.

They repeated his slogans back to him like they were at a concert: \"Money out of politics, money in your pocket and Medicare for all.\"

El-Sayed told the crowd that the campaign against him had been one of the ugliest seen in their lifetime and thanked them for their support. Progressives are celebrating his success as a massive win.

One of them told me that they never want to hear again that progressives can’t win.

Crowd at El-Sayed's campaign party are jubilant
